text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Following the High Court's recent ruling on native title in the Wik case, Queensland, Western Australia and the Northern Territory - the three states most reliant on pastoral industry - will mount a united campaign for special legislation aimed at extingushing native title on leasehold land. Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge said yesterday he would push for a national referendum on the issue if talks with Prime Minister John Howard ruled out the extinguishment of native title. Page 1.

While Monsanto Inc's pest-resistant cotton, the first transgenic crop to be commercially released in Australia, has seen a major reduction in chemical use half way through its growing season, incidents of poor performance have raised concerns. Monsanto Astralia's cotton team leader Richard Jagger reported about 30 of the 350 growers with access to the new strain reported early problems with excessive fruit loss, believed to be the fault of insect attacks. Page 2.

A sharp rise in wool prices has seen the eastern market indicator go through the 600 cent a kilogram mark this week for the first time in four months, closing last night at 617 cents and lifting some of the gloom hanging over the wool industry. But Austrlian Council of Wool Exporters executive director Bob Quirk cautioned the increase was due more to a limited amount of wool being auctioned over the next four weeks than to any real change or lift in demand. Page 4.

Australian Securities Commission chairman Alan Cameron has suggested economic conditions in Australia are again reaching a potential "danger zone" for unscrupulous behaviour if the importance of enforcement sanctions are downgraded. The ASC's second submssion to the Wallis inquiry is aimed at ensuring enforcement is not left out of the reforms currently being drawn up. Page 4.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a suprise move, Lachlan Murdoch and James Packer last night sealed a deal which will see Kerry Packer's Nine Network televise both Super League and the Australian Rugby League competition, sealing Nine as the major free-to-air broadcaster of rugby leage. The deal is set to weaken the ARL's broadcasting advantage, which until now, it held over the game. Page 1.

In a bid to encourage customers to switch to electronic banking, ANZ Bank will impose a A$2 fee for over-the-counter transactions at most branches under a new fee structure which will limit the customer to a maximum of four free transactions per month. Ina further move, ANZ also doubled some account keeping fees from A$2 to A$4. Within hours of the move, the ANZ received support from the other major Australian banks. Page 1.

Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer has set the Government's strongest direction on the native title issue yet by signalling that it could use the backlash generated by the High Court Wik decision to re-examine the basis of the Native Title Act. Fischer has also issued a strong warning to Aboriginal groups that "outlandish" land claims would destroy the reconciliation process. Page 1.

A massive wheat harvest is set to become a record-breaker with a boom for the industry's export harvest bringing much needed financial returns for grain growers and rural communities. Iran has just signed a deal which will see Australia ship a further 1.5 million tonnes to the Middle East and over half of the Australian Wheat Board's 17 million tonne export forecast for the 1996/97 season - which commenced in October - has already been sold. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The New South Wales Government's anticipated coastal policy will now allow sand mining of some sensitive beachside areas in a move which sees the reversal of an election commitment to ban such operations. The policy allows mining companies to proceed if tey can satisfy the requirements of a rigorous assessment which rules that their operations will not adversely affect sand dunes. Page 1.

Yesterday former Prime Minister Paul Keating launched a new service which is the first in the world to offer Internet phone-calls using a standard telephone and without the need for extra computer equipment. The service is tipped to slash both long-distane and international calls by up to 75 per cent on current rates. Page 1.

Australia's youngest convicted criminal, a 10-year-old-boy, who faces another 17 charges including stealing, assault and car theft, has been given a final warning by a New South Wales Children's Court magistrate. The boy, who played with a yo-yo while awating sentence, was yesterday placed on probation for 18 months for stealing and breaching an earlier probation order and was warned that any more trouble would mean time in a detention centre. Page 1.

A panel beater charged with murder over the alleged hit-run death of an 18-year-old woman has been granted A$75,000 bail after he was bashed by four inmates at Parklea jail on Wednesday night. The inmates set upon Brain Hall after details of his recent court appearance were shown on the evening television news. Hall received minor injuries from the attack. Page 3.
THE AGE

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett has attacked the Australian Olympic Committee for its decision to put A$7.3 million into Reef Casino, saying yesterday he was reconsidering whether the Victorian Government should donate money to the AOC, suggesting instead funds may be channelled directly to athletes and sporting bodies. Page A1.

A study by Dr Simon Jackman of the Australian National University, conducted during the 1996 election to incorporate voters and politicians, has revealed a massive gap between "mainstream" Australia and its politicians on race-based issues. There is also a big gap between voters who describe themselves as working class and those who deem themselves middle class, although these sorts of gaps don't exist for any other policy question. Page A2.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics has admitted its new surveying techniques, changing from face to face interviews to phone polling, have underestimated employment growth in Australia, resulting in contradictory news about the job market. Employment Miister Amanda Vanstone seized on the news saying employment may be up 113,000 since the election, rather than the reported estimate of 68,000. Page A3.

Homicide squad detectives said yesterday a 14-year-old boy, missing since Tuesday, may have been murdered or be lying somewhere unable to get help. One man has been charged with the attempted murder of the missing boy, while he and another man have been harged with the false imprisonment of the boy and his 17-year-old brother. Page A3.
